visuals.title: Where it shows
visuals.text: Petechiae and bruising, bleeding gums, haematuria, breathlessness; can progress to multi-organ failure.

Replaces

glossary.Thrombus: A blood clot formed inside a blood vessel.
glossary.Clotting factors: Plasma proteins that work in sequence to form a fibrin clot.
glossary.Coagulation factors: Plasma proteins that work in sequence to form a fibrin clot.
glossary.Trauma: Physical injury to the body, e.g. from a crash or fall.
glossary.Metastatic: Cancer that has spread from where it started to other parts of the body.
glossary.Haematological malignancy: Cancer of blood cells or bone marrow, such as leukaemia or lymphoma.
glossary.Bruising: Bleeding under the skin causing purple-blue discolouration.
glossary.Multi-organ failure: Failure of two or more organ systems, such as kidneys, lungs and liver.
glossary.Organ dysfunction: An organ no longer working properly.
glossary.Shock: Inadequate blood flow to tissues, causing organ failure.
glossary.Blood film: A thin smear of blood examined under the microscope to look at cell shapes.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.IV fluids: Fluids given into a vein to support blood pressure and circulation.
glossary.Coagulation profile: Tests of clotting: PT, APTT, fibrinogen and D-dimer.
glossary.Fibrinogen replacement: Giving fibrinogen, usually as cryoprecipitate, when levels are low.
glossary.Blood products: Components made from donated blood, such as red cells, platelets, FFP and cryoprecipitate.
glossary.Coagulation cascade: The chain of clotting factor reactions that ends in fibrin formation.
glossary.Microcirculation: The smallest blood vessels: arterioles, capillaries and venules.
glossary.Haemostasis: The body's process of stopping bleeding.
glossary.Haemolytic: Relating to the destruction of red blood cells.
glossary.Antibiotics: Drugs that kill or stop the growth of bacteria.
glossary.Fetus: The unborn baby; delivery removes the obstetric trigger.
